conflicts.subject: refund-not-idempotent
conflicts.detail: gateway.refund(charge_id) has no idempotency key (gateway.py:23-25): every call creates a new refund, so a retried cancel or a cancel racing a refund webhook could refund twice.
solutions: Record a refund-requested marker before calling the gateway and never call refund again once it exists
conflicts.recommended: Write a refund marker first; with a marker present, a retry completes the order as refunded without calling the gateway

resolution.decision: D05: refund marker written before gateway.refund; with a marker present a retry completes as refunded without a second gateway call

conflicts.subject: cancel-paid-order
conflicts.detail: C cancels a paid order without refunding it (orders.py:3), so money A charged is kept for a cancelled order; the user requires a cancelled paid order to be refunded exactly once.
solutions: Cancel of a paid order refunds through the gateway and ends in status refunded

resolution.decision: D02 (user requirement in task.md): pending->cancelled; paid->one gateway refund->status refunded with one ledger refund; cancelled/refunded->no-op

conflicts.subject: charge-retry-idempotency
conflicts.detail: A's idempotency key falls back to str(id(order)) and gateway timeouts are not handled: after a timeout that charged, the order stays unpaid and a retry with another key charges twice.
solutions: Require the client key, remember the first key per order and reuse it for every retry
conflicts.recommended: Client key required; first attempted key per order is recorded before the gateway call and reused on every retry; a key used for another order is refused; already-paid orders are never charged

resolution.decision: D03: client key required; first key per order recorded before the charge and reused for every retry; key reuse across orders refused; paid orders never charged; GatewayTimeout re-raised with order left pending and the attempt recorded so a retry collects the original charge

conflicts.subject: webhook-redelivery
conflicts.detail: A applies every webhook delivery again and ignores the type; a duplicate delivery, or a webhook plus the synchronous pay() result, would be applied (and ledgered) twice.
solutions: De-duplicate by event id and make transitions state-checked
Ignore webhooks and rely on pay() only
conflicts.recommended: Record processed event ids atomically with the change; charge.succeeded only moves pending->paid, charge.refunded only paid->refunded; the ledger is appended only on a real transition

resolution.decision: D04: processed event ids stored atomically with the change; state-checked transitions; ledger appended only on a real transition

conflicts.subject: order-payment-state
conflicts.detail: A records payment as a boolean 'paid' flag; C records it as status pending/paid/cancelled/refunded. Two sources of truth can disagree (paid=True while status=cancelled).
solutions: Make Order.status the only payment state and drop A's paid flag
conflicts.recommended: Order.status is the single source of truth; 'paid' is derived (status == paid)

resolution.decision: D01: Order.status is the single payment state; A's paid flag dropped (derived from status)

conflicts.subject: partial-writes
conflicts.detail: No source persists anything; the user requires that a failed store write (StoreError) leaves the order unchanged, and the gateway call cannot be inside the write.
solutions: One atomic write per state change, checked before any mutation; intent markers written before gateway calls
conflicts.recommended: Every state change is one atomic store write (all or nothing); payment and refund intents are written before the gateway call so a retry after a failed write is safe

resolution.decision: D06: one atomic store write per state change (fail check before any mutation); intent records written before gateway calls

conflicts.subject: amount-units
conflicts.detail: A uses order['amount'], B subscription['price'], the task uses amount_cents.

resolution.decision: D07: integer amount_cents everywhere (A amount and B price map to it)

conflicts.subject: renewal-duplication
conflicts.detail: B creates a new order on every renew() call; renewing one period twice would bill the month twice.
conflicts.recommended: renew(subscription, period) returns the existing order for the same subscription id and period

resolution.decision: D08: renew(subscription, period) de-duplicates by subscription id + period

conflicts.subject: order
conflicts.detail: Order exists in A:Order, C:Order; fields not shared: amount_cents (only A), charge_id (only A), paid (only A), status (only C)
solutions: Merge into one table holding the fields kept features need
Keep separate tables if the two only share a name, and rename one
conflicts.recommended: Merge into one entity; list every field's origin in architecture.json

resolution.decision: D09: one Order entity merging A (amount_cents, charge_id) and C (status) fields

conflicts.subject: order.primary-key
conflicts.detail: Order primary key type is not known for A, C; find it before deciding the merged key
solutions: Read the source's schema or migrations for the type
Record it as unknown and decide in the architecture
conflicts.recommended: Find the real type before designing the merged entity

resolution.decision: D10: Order primary key is a generated string id ord_<n>
